title: Relative profinite test schemes: existence, functoriality and site properties
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathbf{Prof}$ consist of compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces and continuous maps in the smaller universe, with coverings the finite jointly surjective families. Let $X$ be any scheme and let $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ be the site of weakly etale $X$-schemes with fpqc coverings [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $S\in\mathbf{Prof}$ and a cofiltered presentation $S=\varprojlim_i S_i$ by finite discrete quotient sets in that universe, the inverse limit $X[S]=\varprojlim_i\coprod_{s\in S_i}X$ exists as an $X$-scheme and is weakly etale over $X$. It is canonically independent of the finite-quotient presentation; continuous maps $S\to T$ induce morphisms $X[S]\to X[T]$, compatible with identities and composition. The resulting functor $u_X:\mathbf{Prof}\to X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ preserves finite limits and sends finite jointly surjective families to fpqc covering families. It also preserves finite disjoint unions. For $X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ there is a canonical functorial identification $X[S]\cong\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{LC}(S,\mathbf Z)$, where $\operatorname{LC}(S,\mathbf Z)$ denotes the ring of locally constant functions with pointwise operations; the identification sends the map induced by $S\to T$ to the spectrum of precomposition.

proof.text: Use the existing concrete functors in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.ModuleObject.Basic: profiniteToScheme is Spec of locally constant integer-valued functions, profiniteToProEt equips this scheme with its weakly etale structure morphism, and profiniteToProEtOf X is its base change along X → Spec Z. The existing source declarations weaklyEtale_toSpecZ_profiniteToScheme and preservesFiniteLimits_profiniteToProEt supply weak etaleness and finite-limit preservation over Spec Z. They are reused as stated obligations, not reproved or asserted to be closed here. MorphismProperty.Over.pullback preserves finite limits, so composition proves the finite-limit clause for every X.

Prove the fpqc-covering assertion first over Spec Z. The closed spectrum theorem identifies each point of Spec LC(T,Z) with (t,p). Given a finite jointly surjective family S_a → T, choose a preimage s of t and use the point (s,p). The formula for evaluation shows directly that its image is (t,p). Each spectrum map is weakly etale: both structure maps to the terminal scheme are weakly etale, and cancel the target structure map using MorphismProperty.of_postcomp. Hence each map is flat. Maps of affine schemes are affine and therefore quasi-compact. A finite jointly surjective family of these quasi-compact flat maps is an fpqc family by QuasiCompactCover.of_finite. Pull back this covering to X using Precoverage.mem_coverings_of_isPullback and the pullback squares of MorphismProperty.Over.pullback. This also handles the empty family without a nonemptiness assumption.

The covering argument over Spec Z, together with weak etaleness of each arrow, proves CoverPreserving for profiniteToProEt directly. A coherent covering sieve of a profinite space contains a finite effective-epimorphic family; Profinite.effectiveEpiFamily_tfae identifies this with joint surjectivity. Push forward that family into the pro-etale precoverage and enlarge its generated sieve. Finite-limit preservation gives representable flatness, hence continuity. Compose with the proved continuity of pro-etale base change to obtain continuity of profiniteToProEtOf X. For any representable of its subcanonical target site, continuity pulls it back to a coherent sheaf, hence to an extensive sheaf, since the extensive topology is below the coherent topology. Mathlib identifies extensive sheaves with finite-product-preserving presheaves. Yoneda then turns these product-preservation statements into preservation of all finite coproducts by the original functor. Apply the same argument after the forgetful functor to Over X.

A finite discrete profinite space S is the coproduct of its points, each a copy of the one-point profinite space. Construct its coproduct cocone explicitly by the constant point inclusions; a map out is obtained by evaluating the chosen component map at the unique point. The preceding coproduct-preservation result gives the unique comparison isomorphism from the coproduct of copies of F(*) to F(S), for F = profiniteToProEtOf X followed by forgetting to Over X. Naturality follows by composing with every coproduct inclusion. Finite-limit preservation identifies F(*) with the terminal object id_X of Over X. Whisker this identification with sigmaConst to obtain exactly the stated natural isomorphism on FintypeCat.

For any cofiltered profinite limit cone with surjective projections, locally constant integer-valued functions form the filtered colimit of the rings at its stages. Profinite.exists_locallyConstant gives the representative at a stage. If two representatives at the same stage agree after pullback, surjectivity of that projection makes them equal already there; this is precisely the injectivity criterion in Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf'. The forgetful functor from commutative rings reflects this filtered colimit. Passing to opposites gives a limiting cone of opposite rings, and Scheme.Spec preserves this limit. Since the indexing category is connected, Over.forget (Spec Z) reflects this limiting cone. Ordinary base change Over.pullback preserves all limits, giving the required limiting cone in Over X. The proof applies in particular to the finite-quotient presentations in the statement.

The unique structure morphism Spec Z → Spec Z is the identity by terminality. Rewrite base change along it using MorphismProperty.Over.pullbackCongr and pullbackId, and whisker with the forgetful functors. This gives the stated functorial identification over Spec Z with profiniteToScheme, whose maps were defined by precomposition from the outset.

lean.statement: theorem profinite_test_object_functor (X : Scheme.{u}) : PreservesFiniteLimits (profiniteToProEtOf X) ∧ (∀ (A : Type u) [Finite A], PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete A) (profiniteToProEtOf X)) ∧ Nonempty (FintypeCat.toProfinite ⋙ profiniteToProEtOf X ⋙ Scheme.ProEt.forget X ≅ forget FintypeCat.{u} ⋙ sigmaConst.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 X))) ∧ (∀ (I : Type u) [SmallCategory I] [IsCofiltered I] (D : I ⥤ FintypeCat.{u}) (c : Cone (D ⋙ FintypeCat.toProfinite)), IsLimit c → (∀ i : I, Function.Surjective (c.π.app i)) → Nonempty (IsLimit ((profiniteToProEtOf X ⋙ Scheme.ProEt.forget X).mapCone c))) ∧ (∀ (A : Type u) [Finite A] (S : A → Profinite.{u}) (T : Profinite.{u}) (f : ∀ a : A, S a ⟶ T), (∀ t : T, ∃ (a : A) (s : S a), f a s = t) → Presieve.ofArrows (fun a ↦ (profiniteToProEtOf X |>.obj (S a)).left) (fun a ↦ (profiniteToProEtOf X |>.map (f a)).left) ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage ((profiniteToProEtOf X).obj T).left) ∧ Nonempty (profiniteToProEtOf specZ.{u} ⋙ Scheme.ProEt.forget specZ ⋙ Over.forget specZ ≅ profiniteToScheme.{u})
